clue.text: Fashionable party men under one roof?

parts.note: something fashionable is 'in'
a do is a party or celebration
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A trendy gathering of men all held together in one building.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the crossword stock abbreviation for men as opposed to officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening inside a building is literally under a single roof; the question mark flags the whimsical phrasing.

clue.text: Helplessness of the old man in Quito centuries ago?

indicators.note: in places the father figure inside the description of old Quito

parts.note: before the Spanish conquest Quito was a city of the Inca empire
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Wondering about a father's frailty in ancient Ecuador.
explanation.walkthrough: Quito, now Ecuador's capital, was once an Inca stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapacity is a lack of ability or strength, the state of being helpless.

clue.text: Rich man's sort of nightclubs?

definitions.meaning: the name traditionally given to the wealthy man in Jesus's parable of Lazarus, from the Latin for 'rich'
seedy, disreputable bars and clubs are called by this slang plural

explanation.surface: A wealthy man's taste in seedy nightspots.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin Vulgate's word for the rich man in Luke 16 became his traditional name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dives is the biblical rich man, and dives are shabby, low-class drinking or music joints.

clue.text: Big swimmer is idiotic crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the idiotic word straddles the river letter

parts.note: oafish means clumsy and stupid

explanation.surface: Some fool trying to swim a big river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The oarfish is a giant ribbon-like deep-sea fish, the longest bony fish known.

clue.text: Meat of Senior Common Room items for discussion, mostly

parts.note: SCR is the standard abbreviation for a university Senior Common Room

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an agenda is the list of items to be discussed at a meeting

explanation.surface: Dons in the Senior Common Room debating the meat on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRAG END is a cheap bony cut from the neck of mutton, familiar in British cooking; 'mostly' drops the last letter of AGENDA.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrag end is a cheap cut of mutton neck, so it is a kind of meat.

clue.text: European control coming throug in broadcast

indicators.note: coming through (printed throug) in broadcast means the word is heard rather than read, as over the airwaves

parts.note: to check something is to control or restrain it

explanation.surface: A continental official exercising control over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A Czech is a native of the Czech Republic, a European nation.

clue.text: Friendly female in a moral tale

indicators.note: in puts the female letter inside the phrase 'a fable'

parts.note: a fable is a short story with a moral

explanation.surface: A kindly woman appearing in one of Aesop's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means pleasant, approachable and good-natured, a close synonym for friendly.

clue.text: Sister in London's business area, one trouble-maker giving voice

indicators.note: in places the sister inside the postcode letters

parts.note: EC, East Central, is the postcode for the City of London financial district
a sister in religious orders is a nun
I is the Roman numeral for one
Ate was the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A nun loose in the City stirring up trouble and speaking out.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London, its financial district, has EC postcodes.
explanation.definitionFit: To enunciate is to pronounce or express clearly, to put words into speech.

clue.text: Yours truly the editor — upstanding judge!

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying 'me'
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor signing off, praising an honest judge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upstanding' turns MEED upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to consider or hold an opinion, as when one judges something to be so.

clue.text: Bird hanging under part of tree died

indicators.note: hanging under puts the bird below the branch, which in a down answer means after it

parts.note: a bough is a main branch of a tree
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird dangling dead from a branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bought it' is British slang for being killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bought it is an informal idiom, from wartime slang, meaning was killed or died.

clue.text: Temporary documentation superfluous, not needed in church

indicators.note: needed in tells us the following pieces must be placed inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England abbreviation
something superfluous is over, left over or surplus
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling that paperwork in church is pointless and not wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed in' puts the pieces inside the church. A cover note is a British insurance term for an interim certificate issued before the full policy.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer's cover note is a provisional certificate giving protection until the formal policy is issued.

clue.text: Bit of luck you'll need following gospel

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
Luke is one of the four Gospels of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A churchgoer saying you need a lucky break after reading scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you'll need' is only a link between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluke is a chance stroke of good fortune, a lucky accident.

clue.text: Giving approval to one beastly male and abnegating responsibility

parts.note: passing a bill or a candidate means approving it
a buck is a male animal such as a deer or rabbit, and 'the' picks out one of them

explanation.surface: Someone nodding through a single stag while dodging their own duties.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from poker, where a marker called the buck showed who was to deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass the buck is the idiom for shifting blame or duty onto someone else, disowning one's own obligation.

clue.text: Decent boss somehow not quite the ideal?

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A decent manager who somehow falls short of perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-best is just below the top choice, so short of the ideal.

clue.text: Tom maybe taken to church as fellow hooked for matrimony?

indicators.note: taken to says the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A man called Tom led to church as a groom caught for a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but is a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: A good catch is a desirable marriage partner, someone landed like a fish on the hook.

clue.text: Heroes met to go out in small group

indicators.note: to go out suggests the letters break from their order and go astray

explanation.surface: Champions meeting up to head out on the town in a little party.
explanation.definitionFit: A threesome is a group of three people, a trio.

clue.text: Commercial brand dear, meant to be special

indicators.note: special here signals the letters are put into a specially made new order

explanation.surface: A sweet note about a branded product meant to feel special to you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges the letters of DEAR MEANT; 'to be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name is the name under which a product is sold commercially, a brand name.

clue.text: When I have trimmed outside of garment that's rubbing

indicators.note: outside of means the 'when' word wraps around the garment

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
a bra is an undergarment
the contraction of 'I have', with the HA cut away

explanation.surface: A complaint about an ill-fitting garment chafing once it was cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrasive scrapes or grinds against a surface, wearing it by friction.

clue.text: Soldiers going between Dartmoor landmarks, a cause of suffering

indicators.note: going between means the soldiers sit in the middle, separating the two landmarks

parts.note: tors are the rocky hilltop outcrops for which Dartmoor is famous; two of them are needed
men is a stock synonym for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops marching between rocky peaks on a bleak moor, a grim ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a moorland in Devon, south-west England, dotted with granite hilltops called tors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is one who inflicts pain or distress, so is a source of suffering.

clue.text: Sort to join the Green Party? One lives in a particular place

definitions.text: One lives in a particular place

indicators.note: to join says the sort piece is attached to the green piece

parts.note: eco is the prefix for anything environmentally green
a type is a sort or kind

explanation.surface: A kind of person who'd sign up with the environmentalists.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology an ecotype is a variety of a species adapted to a specific local habitat.

clue.text: One embarrassed in company to reveal statement of beliefs

indicators.note: in places the blushing piece inside the company letters

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A shy person among colleagues finally declaring what they believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reveal' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo, from Latin 'I believe', is a creed or set of guiding principles.

clue.text: Something that sticks out — leg and good to hide hair!

indicators.note: to hide means the good letter is concealed inside the jutting feature

parts.note: a chin sticks out from the face
on, or leg, is the cricket term for the half of the field behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: A protruding leg and a good attempt to conceal one's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A chignon is a knot or coil of hair worn at the nape of the neck, a hairstyle.

clue.text: Uncontrollable moods — medicines may be got rid of!

indicators.note: uncontrollable suggests letters running wild into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Wild mood swings may mean the pills get thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncontrollable' rearranges MOODS MEDICINES; 'may be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment or ships that are decommissioned are withdrawn from service, effectively disposed of.

clue.text: Hawthorn blossom's picked up in this grass

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal

parts.note: may is the old name for hawthorn blossom; the 's makes it plural-sounding

explanation.surface: Hawthorn petals gathered from a field of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The cereal crop also called corn is botanically a member of the grass family.

clue.text: Foreign bread upset some vegetarians

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top
some means only part of the word's letters are used

explanation.surface: Imported loaves that offended some non-meat-eaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money: the answer is Nigeria's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and the naira is the currency of Nigeria.

clue.text: Virginia politician is seductive woman

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Virginian politician revealed as a femme fatale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A vamp is a woman who uses her charms to seduce men, a femme fatale.

clue.text: Anguish of some about match

indicators.note: about means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
a go is a turn or bout, a contest or match

explanation.surface: Fans in torment over a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony and anguish are synonyms for extreme mental or physical suffering.

clue.text: Name used for Conservative in abuse is original

indicators.note: used for means the name letter stands in place of the Conservative letter

parts.note: invective is abusive, insulting language

explanation.surface: A Tory insulted with a fresh, creative label in a political slanging match.
explanation.walkthrough: In INVECTIVE the C is swapped for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inventive is creative and original, coming up with new ideas.

clue.text: Came first showing power, then dropped back

parts.note: receded means withdrew or fell back

explanation.surface: A frontrunner showed strength early, then faded in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' and 'then' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to go before, so something that preceded came earlier in order.

clue.text: Youngster one books, enthusiast getting absorbed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: getting absorbed means the enthusiast is taken inside the books letters

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A keen reader soaking up one book after another.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, a youngster in the earliest years.
